{1–6} God swears by these great signs, by the soul that attains success and by other souls that are wicked, saying: {By the sun and its brightness}; that is, its light and the benefit that comes forth from it. {By the moon when it follows it}; that is, it follows it in its stations and its light. {By the day when it displays it}; that is, it reveals what is on the surface of the earth and makes it clear. {By the night when it covers it}; that is, it covers the surface of the earth, so that what is upon it becomes dark. The alternation of darkness and light, and of the sun and the moon, over this world, with regularity, precision, and maintenance of the interests of the servants, is the greatest proof that God is All-Knowing of everything and All-Powerful over everything, and that He alone is the One worthy of worship, and that every deity other than Him is false. {By the heaven and He who built it}: it may be that "mā" is a relative pronoun, so the oath is by the heaven and its Builder, who is God, Exalted is He; and it may be that "mā" is a verbal noun, so the oath is by the heaven and its construction, which is the utmost that can be conceived of in firmness, precision, and excellence. Similar to this is His saying: {And the earth and He who spread it out}; that is, He extended it and widened it, so that creation is then able to benefit from it in all the ways of benefit.

{7–8} {And a soul and He who proportioned it}: it may be that the intended meaning is: and the soul of all the animal creatures, as the generality supports this; and it may be that the oath is by the soul of the accountable human being, as indicated by what follows. In any case, the soul is a great sign among His signs, deserving of oaths by it; for it is in the utmost subtlety and lightness, swift in movement, activity, change, being affected, and psychological emotions such as concern, will, intention, love, and hatred. It is the soul which, were it not for it, the body would be a mere statue with no benefit in it. Its proportioning as it is, is one of the great signs of God.

{9–10} His saying: {He has succeeded who purifies it}; that is, one who purifies his soul from sins, cleanses it from defects, elevates it through obedience to God, and exalts it with beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. {And he has failed who corrupts it}; that is, one who conceals his noble soul, which is not worthy of being suppressed and concealed, by defiling it with vices and approaching defects and sins, abandoning what would perfect and develop it, and practicing what would disgrace and corrupt it.

{11–15} {Thamud denied in their transgression}; that is, because of their rebellion, their arrogance against the truth, and their insolence toward their messenger. {When the most wretched of them was sent forth}; that is, the most wretched of the tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, for the slaughter of the she-camel, when they agreed upon that and commanded him, and he complied with them. {Then the Messenger of God said to them}: Salih, peace be upon him, warning: {The she-camel of God and her drink}; that is, beware of slaughtering the she-camel of God, which He made for you as a great sign, and do not repay God's blessing upon you by slaughtering her who gives you milk. Similar to this is His saying: {And the earth and He who spread it out}; that is, He extended it and widened it, so that creation is then able to benefit from it in all the ways of benefit.

{7–8} {And a soul and He who proportioned it}: it may be that the intended meaning is: and the soul of all the animal creatures, as the generality supports this; and it may be that the oath is by the soul of the accountable human being, as indicated by what follows. In any case, the soul is a great sign among His signs, deserving of oaths by it; for it is in the utmost subtlety and lightness, swift in movement, activity, change, being affected, and psychological emotions such as concern, will, intention, love, and hatred. It is the soul which, were it not for it, the body would be a mere statue with no benefit in it. Its proportioning as it is, is one of the great signs of God.

{9–10} His saying: {He has succeeded who purifies it}; that is, one who purifies his soul from sins, cleanses it from defects, elevates it through obedience to God, and exalts it with beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. {And he has failed who corrupts it}; that is, one who conceals his noble soul, which is not worthy of being suppressed and concealed, by defiling it with vices and approaching defects and sins, abandoning what would perfect and develop it, and practicing what would disgrace and corrupt it.

{11–15} {Thamud denied in their transgression}; that is, because of their rebellion, their arrogance against the truth, and their insolence toward their messenger. {When the most wretched of them was sent forth}; that is, the most wretched of the tribe, who was Qudar ibn Salif, for the slaughter of the she-camel, when they agreed upon that and commanded him, and he complied with them. {Then the Messenger of God said to them}: Salih, peace be upon him, warning: {The she-camel of God and her drink}; that is, beware of slaughtering the she-camel of God, which He made for you as a great sign, and do not repay God's blessing upon you by slaughtering her who gives you milk. But they denied their prophet Salih. {So they slaughtered her, and their Lord blanketed them [with destruction] for their sin}; that is, He destroyed them, enveloped them with His punishment, and sent upon them the cry from above them and the quake from beneath them, so they became prostrate upon their knees, and you would find none of them calling or answering. {And He made them equal}: upon them; that is, He made them equal in the punishment. {And He does not fear its consequence}; that is, its aftermath. And how could one fear who is subduing, and none of creation can escape His subjugation and control? He is the Wise in all that He decrees and legislates.

[Completed, and praise be to God.]

This surah is Meccan.
